title: Lambda Cold Start and Init Duration Latency

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.5.2 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.5.2 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudwatch` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" namespace="AWS/Lambda" metric_name="InitDuration"
| table _time metric_name namespace unit average maximum
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.5.2_lambda_cold_start_and_in_2"
| sort -_time
description: Cold starts add tail latency to user-facing APIs and batch jobs; tracking Init Duration guides memory tuning, provisioned concurrency, and VPC design.
value: Detecting lambda cold start and init duration latency early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Collect the `InitDuration` CloudWatch metric for each function. For log-based validation, subscribe Lambda log groups to Splunk and parse `REPORT` lines for `Init Duration`. Baseline p95/p99 init time per function and alert when cold-start latency breaches SLO after deploys or scaling events.
visualization: Line chart (avg/max Init Duration by function), Box plot or percentile overlay (if precomputed), Table (FunctionName, p95 init ms).
knownFalsePositives: Cold starts, retries, and a bad client sending junk traffic can all raise error counts without a code bug. We look at the share of invocations and we compare the same time last week before we assume the function is broken.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:cloudwatch`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.5.16.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `metric_name` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Collect the `InitDuration` CloudWatch metric for each function. For log-based validation, subscribe Lambda log groups to Splunk and parse `REPORT` lines for `Init Duration`. Baseline p95/p99 init time per function and alert when cold-start latency breaches SLO after deploys or scaling events.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" namespace="AWS/Lambda" metric_name="InitDuration"
| table _time metric_name namespace unit average maximum
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.5.2_lambda_cold_start_and_in_2"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudwatch` in `index=aws` to detect lambda cold start and init duration latency. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the Amazon CloudWatch console Metrics for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `metric_name` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_5_2_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Line chart (avg/max Init Duration by function), Box plot or percentile overlay (if precomputed), Table (FunctionName, p95 init ms)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of lambda cold start and init duration latency so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
